title: Tool definition
description: What a tool must declare before it is allowed on a surface. Tool selection is a writing problem before it is a code problem — a model picks from the description, and no implementation quality recovers a vague one.

name.description: verb_noun, lower snake case, imperative. Where a server spans several resource families, prefix by resource so the model can tell them apart. Either way the name must disclose whether the call CREATES something.

description.description: EXACTLY THREE SENTENCES: what it does · when to use it · when NOT to use it. The third prevents mis-selection and is the one everyone omits — a model choosing between two plausible tools has nothing to separate them unless each says why it is not the other.

requires.description: Preconditions, stated explicitly. Models call tools out of order unless the description forbids it.

onPartialSuccess.description: What a half-success looks like, so the model reports it rather than claiming a clean run.

inputSchema.description: Constrain as narrowly as the domain allows. A model will confidently produce a plausible value that does not exist — an enum catches that BEFORE the call, which is the cheapest place.

sideEffect.description: read = no change. create = NOT safely repeatable, needs an idempotency key. update/delete = changes existing state, needs preview+confirm.

previewTool.description: Required when sideEffect is not 'read'. The partner tool that returns what WOULD change and nothing else.

idempotencyKey.description: Required when sideEffect is 'create'. The caller supplies it, derived from INTENT — never random, never a timestamp. A random key is worse than no key, because it creates the appearance of protection.

blastRadius.description: The worst outcome of one confirmed call, in plain language a non-engineer can weigh.

timeoutMs.description: Every wait is bounded. An unbounded wait GUARANTEES the client timeout that causes a retry — which is how duplicate work happens.

failureTest.description: Path to the test asserting the FAILURE path. A tool without one is not done.

examples.name: validate_addin

description.what: Checks a built add-in against the four rejection causes before submission.
description.when: Use before packaging or submitting, and after any manifest or entitlement change.
description.whenNot: Not for building. Call build_all_versions first if no output exists yet.
requires: A completed build for at least one target version
description.onPartialSuccess: Returns every finding it can reach even if one check errors; surface the warnings array rather than reporting a clean run.

examples.blastRadius: None. Reads files and makes one outbound HTTP HEAD request.
